title: Enforce Circle parent privacy and bound remote QR logo reads
detail: The existing privileged Circle store loads parent metadata and fresh canonical viewer capabilities; the parent-access module is a pure gate with no additional admin-client adoption. Privileged Circle shell reads now check the owning Space status, visibility and canonical Circles module switch before reading a roster or returning identity. Active private Space viewers retain enabled-module access, while canonical writers/staff retain disabled-module stewardship; legacy unpartitioned Circles retain their existing behavior. Circle autocomplete uses the authenticated session client so parent and Circle RLS filters run before the result limit. Remote QR logo reads pin the validated DNS address into a dedicated native HTTPS connection lookup, retaining the original hostname for TLS/SNI verification and disabling pooled sockets. Every redirect/non-success is rejected, HTTPS-only applies even to resolved root-relative assets, and a four-second deadline covers DNS through response completion. Reads consume a stream with a 512KB retained-byte bound and cancellation, instead of allocating an unlimited arrayBuffer before checking its size. Offline regressions exercise actual shell and route consumers, private-parent denial, writer exceptions, redirect failure, private DNS, streamed bounds and successful image inlining. No live network exploit, database mutation, production behavior or applied-policy verification is claimed. IPv4-mapped private IPv6 forms are canonicalized and rejected before connection. No second DNS lookup is used for the connection. Production deployment and database-policy verification remain release gates.

verify.note: Cheap source wiring guard. Separate focused run: seven suites /138 assertions pass, including controlled DNS, fetch, session and database behavior. No actual internal or external endpoints contacted. Local proof only; full release checks remain separate.
